prompt: A fresh cluster has an Ingress applied and no ingress controller installed. What routes the traffic for it?
hint: Kubernetes ships the object, not the thing that obeys it.

choices.why: kube-proxy routes Service addresses; it never reads an Ingress.

choices.text: The API server, which stores the rules
choices.why: Storing the object is all it does with it.
Right. An Ingress is a request; without a controller it is accepted and ignored.

choices.text: CoreDNS, by pointing the host at a Service
choices.why: CoreDNS answers cluster names; the Ingress host is not one of them.

prompt: The Ingress sends `/admin` to `admin` and `/` to `shop`. A request for `shop.example.test/admin` matches both. Where did it go?

choices.why: Order in the file does not decide; the controller prefers the longest match.
Right: the reply said `admin 1.0`.
Each request reaches one backend, chosen by the rule.
Overlap is normal; it is how a site nests sections.

prompt: An Ingress with `ingressClassName: nginx` was applied in a cluster with only Traefik. What told Ana that nobody was serving it?
hint: The API server saw nothing wrong.

choices.why: It printed `created`; the object is only data.

choices.text: A warning event on the Ingress
choices.why: No component was watching that class, so nobody wrote one.

choices.text: The empty `ADDRESS` column, which was different from the working one
choices.why: Traefik publishes no address here, so both rows were empty and looked alike.

choices.text: Only the `404` when she asked for its host
choices.why: Right. Nothing reports an Ingress nobody adopts; the Gateway API's status conditions are the improvement.

prompt: Match each Gateway API object with who usually writes it.
hint: The table at the start of the section.

pairs.right: The people who run the cluster
The team that owns the application

right_distractors: The API server, from the Ingress

prompt: The HTTPRoute sends `/admin` to `admin` only with the header `X-Staff: yes`. What did a request for `/admin` without the header reach?
hint: The first rule needs both matches.

choices.why: The route has a fallback rule with no matches, which caught it.

choices.text: The shop, through the fallback rule
choices.why: Right: `shop 1.0` answered; only with the header did `admin` answer.
Matches inside one rule must all hold.
No route points there.

prompt: Why does a cluster need the Gateway API's CRDs installed before any of its objects can be applied?
hint: Count the API resources a fresh cluster knows (lesson 2).

choices.text: The types are not built into Kubernetes; the CRDs add them
choices.why: Right. Lesson 43 shows how a CRD adds a type to the API.

choices.text: The CRDs contain the controller's program
choices.why: A CRD defines a type; the controller is a separate Deployment.
Both ran side by side in this lesson.
Its core types are `v1`.

prompt: Which controller should carry out an Ingress is named by the field `___`.
Which of these can an HTTPRoute express in its standard fields, without controller-specific annotations? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: A match on a request header
choices.why: Right: `X-Staff: yes`.

choices.text: Splitting traffic between Services by weight
choices.why: Right: lesson 36 uses it for a canary.

choices.text: Which node the controller runs on
choices.why: That is the controller's own Deployment, not a route.
Right: `PathPrefix /admin`.

choices.text: The image the Service's pods run
choices.why: Routes point at Services; pods are their own business.
